page: Amazon Web Services i3en.24xlarge is an enterprise storage-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The system provides 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores via Intel Xeon 8259CL processors operating at 3.1 GHz, with support for AVX-512 and hardware cryptographic instructions. Memory capacity stands at 768 GB of DDR4 operating at 3 GHz, delivering an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. A central differentiator of this instance is its massive integrated storage array, providing 60,000 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity alongside a 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, configured without discrete GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations confirm the system orientation toward parallel scaling and high data throughput. Multi-core execution demonstrates top-tier capability, reflected in a stress-ng score of 81,307.29 and a PassMark CPU score of 55,934.8. The memory and storage subsystems exhibit high transactional efficiency, registering 21,592.03 on PassMark database operations and over 75.3 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 219.74 GB/sec, supporting static web serving rates of 45.13 GB/sec.

Architectural tradeoffs appear primarily in single-threaded tasks and generative AI. Single-core stress-ng tests and gzip compression throughput settle in the bottom quartile, and LLM text generation speeds are weak due to the absence of dedicated accelerator hardware. From a qualitative resource density perspective, bundling extensive local NVMe storage, significant memory, and 100 Gbps networking minimizes network storage overhead, positioning the instance effectively for distributed NoSQL databases, search clusters, Kafka pipelines, and massive in-memory caching systems.
description: Amazon Web Services i3en.24xlarge is a storage-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor, engineered for high-throughput, data-heavy workloads. It features 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores using Intel Xeon 8259CL processors clocked at 3.1 GHz, paired with 768 GB of DDR4 memory. Bundling 60,000 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and 100 Gbps baseline networking without discrete GPUs, it yields exceptional aggregate I/O and processing capacity. Benchmark data demonstrates top-tier multi-threaded processing, robust database operations, and high Redis SET transaction rates exceeding 75 million operations per second, alongside strong static web serving throughput. However, single-threaded performance and LLM text generation metrics fall into lower tiers, reflecting an architecture focused on parallel scale rather than single-core speed. With high storage and memory density per node, it delivers strong cost efficiency for large relational databases, distributed NoSQL clusters, search indexes, and in-memory caching platforms.
